# When git exits 0 but writes to stderr (status messages, not errors),
# the Exec wrapper must preserve exit code 0 and surface stderr as data,
# not as a failure signal.

exec git init -b main repo
cd repo
exec git config user.email t@t
exec git config user.name t
exec git config commit.gpgsign false
exec git commit --allow-empty -m initial

# `git checkout -b feature` writes "Switched to a new branch 'feature'"
# to stderr and exits 0.
exec git.Exec checkout -b feature
stderr 'Switched to'
